query: what happens to unused material still in stock when a supplier is disqualified
note: THE CROSS-DOCUMENT CASE, and the reason sop_id is null here and nowhere else in the supplier set. With no filter the query competes against both revisions of SOP-QC-014 as well as the whole of SOP-SCM-004. This is the case that would have been impossible before 2026-09-12, when the corpus was one SOP and every query trivially found the only document there was. §6.2 is the immediate-quarantine rule.

query: may we accept a delivery from a supplier after their disqualification date
note: The rule behind the walk's own headline finding: MLOT-2606-0055 arrived 2026-06-24, a month after the 2026-05-20 disqualification, and is still flagged released. §6.2 says goods receipt is blocked and such a receipt owes a deviation against the receipt itself. If retrieval cannot surface this clause, N2's answer can report the anomaly but cannot say which rule it breaks.

query: does a disqualification require a traceability assessment of material already consumed
note: Rev 5's headline change, in the words of the seed's own change note. §7.1 is the scope clause — all lots regardless of disposition, per 21 CFR 211.192. Deliberately expects §7.1 and not the §7 preamble: the preamble says the assessment is required, §7.1 says how far it reaches, and the second is the one that answers the question.

query: when does an affected batch need a recall rather than notifying the customer
note: The clause the answer schema's RECALL_VERDICT rule exists to protect. The tool does not decide a recall and the schema forbids the sentence; §7.3 is what the model must quote instead of deciding. Note this is §7.3 of a DIFFERENT document from the §7.3 the release cases turn on — the label grammar is what keeps those apart.

query: how quickly must lots that reached a hospital be assessed after a supplier is disqualified
note: Five working days, against a disqualification on 2026-05-20 and a today of 2026-09-12 — about four months overdue. That finding exists nowhere in the six databases; it needs this clause. A retrieval miss here makes the overdue assessment invisible again.

query: training required before a qualified person may certify a batch
note: THE REGRESSION GUARD for the acceptance case. This exact retrieval is what rel-001 depends on, and §P4a records it returning first for one phrasing and second for another, behind '3. Responsibilities' — which is why the check is 'in the top k' and not 'at rank 1'. Rev 6 §7.3 is deliberately NOT rejected: see the note in run-retrieval.ts on why a sibling revision is not an intruder.

query: what must a qualified person confirm before certifying for the european union
note: THE CASE THAT PROVES SUPERSEDED REVISIONS STAY REACHABLE. Both revisions have a §7.2 and both are correct retrievals — Rev 6 governed every certification between 2023-07-01 and 2026-02-28, and rel-007 asks about exactly such an act. Deciding WHICH governs is inForceOn's job, applied after retrieval and unit-checked by tools:check. Retrieval's job is to hand over both. A suite that expected only the current revision here would be measuring the date filter and calling it retrieval.

query: repeat test after an out of specification result without an investigation
note: Behind rel-006 (T7): dissolution retested to a pass with no OOS investigation. §6.1 is the clause that says a repeat test without the SOP-QC-003 investigation does not satisfy the section, irrespective of its result. Included because it is the one release case whose governing clause is NOT in section 7, so a retriever that had quietly learned to favour one part of the document would show up here.
